subtopic: Magnetic potential energy of a dipole
stem: The magnetic potential energy, when a magnetic bar of magnetic moment \( \vec{m} \) is placed perpendicular to the magnetic field \( \vec{B} \) is
solution:
Potential energy stored in external magnetic field is given by \( U = -\vec{m}\cdot\vec{B} \)
\( \because \) Angle between \( \vec{m} \) and \( \vec{B} \) is 90°
\( \therefore U = -mB\cos 90° = 0 \)

subject: Physics
stem: A bob is whirled in a horizontal circle by means of a string at an initial speed of 10 rpm. If the tension in the string is quadrupled while keeping the radius constant, the new speed is:
solution:
In horizontal circular motion,
\( T = m\omega^2 r \)
For constant \( m \) and \( r \), \( T \propto \omega^2 \)
\( T' = 4T \) (Given)
\( \Rightarrow \omega' = 2\omega = 20 \) rpm

stem: A metal cube of side 5 cm is charged with 6 \( \mu \)C. The surface charge density on the cube is
solution:
In metal all the charge is present on surface.
\( Q = 6\ \mu C \)
Total surface area \( S = 6a^2 = 6 \times (5 \times 10^{-2})^2 = 6 \times 25 \times 10^{-4} = 150 \times 10^{-4}\ m^2 \)
Surface charge density \( \sigma = \dfrac{Q}{S} = \dfrac{6 \times 10^{-6}}{150 \times 10^{-4}} = 0.4 \times 10^{-3} \) C m\(^{-2}\)

subject: Physics
stem: An ideal fluid is flowing in a non-uniform cross-sectional tube \( XY \) (as shown in the figure) from end \( X \) to end \( Y \). If \( K_1 \) and \( K_2 \) are the kinetic energy per unit volume of the fluid at \( X \) and \( Y \) respectively, then the correct option is :
solution:
According to Bernoulli's principle,
Kinetic energy per unit volume + Potential energy per unit volume + Pressure = Constant
\( \dfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2 + \rho g h + P = \) constant
Apply Bernoulli's principle at point \( X \) and \( Y \),
\( P + K_1 + \rho g(0) = P + K_2 + \rho g(h) \)
\( K_1 = K_2 + \rho g h \)
\( K_1 > K_2 \)

subject: Physics
stem: The escape velocity for earth is \( v \). A planet having 9 times mass that of earth and radius, 16 times that of earth, has the escape velocity of:
solution:
Escape velocity of object from planet is given by
\( (v_e)_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_p}{R_p}} \)
\( \therefore (v_e)_p \propto \sqrt{\dfrac{M_p}{R_p}} \)
Now, \( M_p = 9M_e \) and \( R_p = 16R_e \) (given)
\( \dfrac{(v_e)_p}{(v_e)_e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_p}{R_p} \times \dfrac{R_e}{M_e}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9M_e}{16R_e} \times \dfrac{R_e}{M_e}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{16}} = \dfrac{3}{4} \)
\( \Rightarrow (v_e)_p = \dfrac{3}{4}v \)

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
stem: An electron and an alpha particle are accelerated by the same potential difference. Let \( \lambda_e \) and \( \lambda_\alpha \) denote the de-Broglie wavelengths of the electron and the alpha particle, respectively, then:
solution:
de-Broglie wavelength is given by
\( \lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}} \)
For same potential difference
\( \lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{mq}} \)
\( \dfrac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_e q_e}{m_\alpha q_\alpha}} \)
\( \because m_\alpha \ggg m_e \)
\( \lambda_e > \lambda_\alpha \)

subject: Physics
stem: An object moving along horizontal \( x \)-direction with kinetic energy 10 J is displaced through \( x = \left(3\hat{i}\right) \) m by the force \( \vec{F} = \left(-2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\right) \) N. The kinetic energy of the object at the end of the displacement \( x \) is
solution:
Work energy theorem,
\( W_{all} = \Delta K.E \) (\( W_{all} = \) work done by all forces)
\( \Rightarrow K_f - K_i = \vec{F}\cdot\Delta\vec{x} \)
\( \Rightarrow K_f - 10 = \left(-2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\right)\cdot\left(3\hat{i}\right) \)
\( K_f - 10 = -6 \)
\( K_f = 4 \) J

subject: Physics
stem: An object falls from a height of 10 m above the ground. After striking the ground it loses 50% of its kinetic energy. The height upto which the object can rebounce from the ground is:
solution:
K.E. just before striking the ground \( K_1 = mgh_1 = mg(10) \)
K.E. just after striking the ground \( = K_1 - \dfrac{50}{100}K_1 = \dfrac{50}{100}K_1 = \dfrac{K_1}{2} = K_2 \)
Now, \( K_2 = mgh_2 \)
\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{K_1}{2} = mgh_2 \)
\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{mg(10)}{2} = mgh_2 \Rightarrow h_2 = 5 \) m

stem: In the circuit shown below, the inductance \( L \) is connected to an ac source. The current flowing in the circuit is \( I = I_0\sin\omega t \). The voltage drop \( (V_L) \) across \( L \) is
solution:
\( V_L \) leads current \( I \) by \( \dfrac{\pi}{2} \)
\( \therefore V_L = V_0\sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \quad (\because I = I_0\sin\omega t) \)
\( V_0 = I_0 X_L \)
\( \Rightarrow V_L = I_0 X_L\cos(\omega t) = I_0\omega L\cos(\omega t) \)

stem: A uniform wire of diameter \( d \) carries a current of 100 mA when the mean drift velocity of electrons in the wire is \( v \). For a wire of diameter \( \dfrac{d}{2} \) of the same material to carry a current of 200 mA, the mean drift velocity of electrons in the wire is
solution:
current \( i = nAv_d e \) (\( v_d = \) mean drift velocity)
\( = n\left(\dfrac{\pi D^2}{4}\right)v_d e \)
\( \therefore i \propto D^2 v_d \)
\( \dfrac{100}{200} = \dfrac{(d)^2}{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)^2} \times \dfrac{v}{v'} \)
\( \Rightarrow v' = 2 \times 2^2 v = 8v \)

subject: Physics
stem: In an electrical circuit, the voltage is measured as \( V = (200 \pm 4) \) volt and the current is measured as \( I = (20 \pm 0.2) \) A. The value of the resistance is:
solution:
\( R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{200}{20} = 10\ \Omega \)
\( \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I} = \dfrac{4}{200} + \dfrac{0.2}{20} = \dfrac{4+2}{200} = \dfrac{6}{200} \)
\( \Rightarrow \Delta R = \dfrac{6}{200} \times R = \dfrac{6}{20} = \dfrac{3}{10} = 0.3\ \Omega \)
\( \therefore \) Resistance \( = R \pm \Delta R = (10 \pm 0.3)\ \Omega \)

stem: A step up transformer is connected to an ac mains supply of 220 V to operate at 11000 V, 88 watt. The current in the secondary circuit, ignoring the power loss in the transformer, is
solution:

\( \Rightarrow 88 = 11000\, i \)
\( \Rightarrow i = \dfrac{88}{11 \times 10^3} = 8 \times 10^{-3} \) A
\( \Rightarrow i = 8 \) mA

subject: Physics
stem: A particle is moving along \( x \)-axis with its position \( (x) \) varying with time \( (t) \) as \( x = \alpha t^4 + \beta t^2 + \gamma t + \delta \). The ratio of its initial velocity to its initial acceleration, respectively, is:
solution:
Position of particle, \( x = \alpha t^4 + \beta t^2 + \gamma t + \delta \)
Velocity \( v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 4\alpha t^3 + 2\beta t + \gamma \)
Initial velocity \( = v(t=0) = \gamma \)
Acceleration \( a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = 12\alpha t^2 + 2\beta \)
Initial acceleration \( = a(t=0) = 2\beta \)
\( \therefore \dfrac{v(t=0)}{a(t=0)} = \dfrac{\gamma}{2\beta} \)

stem: The radius of gyration of a solid sphere of mass 5 kg about \( XY \) is 5 m as shown in figure. The radius of the sphere is \( \dfrac{5x}{\sqrt{7}} \) m, then the value of \( x \) is:
solution:
\( I_{XY} = I_{CM} + MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5} \times 5R^2 = 7R^2 \quad ...(1) \)
\( I_{XY} = MK^2 = 5 \times 5^2 \quad ...(2) \)
\( \therefore 5 \times 5^2 = 7 \times R^2 \) [From (1) and (2)]
\( \Rightarrow R = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{7}} \times 5 = \dfrac{5x}{\sqrt{7}} \) (Given)
\( \therefore x = \sqrt{5} \)

stem: Let us consider two solenoids \( A \) and \( B \), made from same magnetic material of relative permeability \( \mu_r \) and equal area of cross-section. Length of \( A \) is twice that of \( B \) and the number of turns per unit length in \( A \) is half that of \( B \). The ratio of self inductances of the two solenoids, \( L_A : L_B \) is
solution:
\( L = \mu_0\mu_r \times n \times A \times N = \mu_0\mu_r n \times A \times \dfrac{N}{l} \times l = \mu_0\mu_r \times n^2 \times A \times l \Rightarrow L \propto n^2 l \)
\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \dfrac{n_A^2}{n_B^2} \times \dfrac{l_A}{l_B} \)
\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \)

stem: According to the law of equipartition of energy, the number of vibrational modes of a polyatomic gas of constant \( \gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v} \) is (\( C_P \) where \( C_V \) are the specific heat capacities of the gas at constant pressure and constant volume, respectively):
solution:
A polyatomic gas has 3 translational, 3 rotational and \( f \) vibration modes
\( U = \dfrac{3}{2}k_B T + \dfrac{3}{2}k_B T + f k_B T \)
\( U = (3 + f)k_B T \)
\( C_v = (3 + f)R \)
\( C_p = (4 + f)R \)
\( \dfrac{C_p}{C_v} = \dfrac{4 + f}{3 + f} = \gamma \)
\( 4 + f = 3\gamma + f\gamma \)
\( 4 - 3\gamma = f(\gamma - 1) \Rightarrow f = \dfrac{4 - 3\gamma}{\gamma - 1} \)

subject: Physics
stem: The amplitude of the charge oscillating in a circuit decreases exponentially as \( Q = Q_0 e^{-Rt/2L} \), where \( Q_0 \) is the charge at \( t = 0 \) s. The time at which charge amplitude decreases to \( 0.50\, Q_0 \) is nearly: [Given that \( R = 1.5\ \Omega, L = 12 \) mH, \( \ln(2) = 0.693 \)]
solution:
Given \( Q = Q_0 e^{-Rt/2L} \)
\( R = 1.5\ \Omega, L = 12 \) mH, \( \ln(2) = 0.693 \)
\( Q = 0.5Q_0, t = ? \)
\( 0.5Q_0 = Q_0 e^{-Rt/2L} \)
\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2} = e^{-Rt/2L} \)
Taking log on both sides
\( \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \ln e^{-Rt/2L} \)
\( \Rightarrow \ln 2 = \dfrac{Rt}{2L} \)
\( t = \dfrac{2L\ln 2}{R} = \dfrac{2 \times 12 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.693}{1.5} \)
\( t = 11.09 \) ms
